speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing fatigue and difficulty concentrating, along with some abnormal blood findings. To understand what is going on, can you tell me your age and sex?

speaker: Patient
text: 53-year-old male. The patient has a 3-week history of fatigue, difficulty to concentrate, and dyspnea on exertion. He also experiences dizziness and digital pain that improves with cold. He has a long history of smoking.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful. You mentioned digital pain that improves with cold; does this occur on your fingers or your toes, and do your digits look white or blue when the pain starts? Also, have you noticed any color changes in your fingertips, such as turning pale or blue?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fatigue and difficulty to concentrate. I also have Dyspnea on exertion, Dizziness, Digital pain that improves with cold.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Raynaud's phenomenon secondary to Polyarteritis Nodosa (PAN).

The combination of fatigue, dyspnea on exertion, dizziness, and digital pain relieved by cold exposure in a 53-year-old smoker is highly suggestive of systemic vasculitis. Can you confirm if the pain in your digits occurs in episodes triggered by stress or cold, and do you have any history of high blood pressure or renal issues?
